newsitem.title: CHINA: China's stock indices end up as concerns ease.
newsitem.headline: China's stock indices end up as concerns ease.

text.p: China's B share indices ended up on Monday in line with sharp rises in the A share markets, boosted by speculative buying as concerns about possible anti-speculative measures eased, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index closed up 0.65 percent to 70.898 points on turnover of $8.2 million against $12 million last Friday.
Shenzhen's B index gained 2.98 percent to close at 169.99 points on turnover of HK$141.8 million ($18.3 million) compared with HK$150.3 million on Friday.
"Investor confidence recovered because Beijing did not announce any new anti-speculation policies at the weekend," an analyst with China Guotai Securities Co said.
Talk that Beijing planned to tighten rules on stock trading cooled market sentiment late last week, brokers said.
Shanghai's A share index jumped 2.96 percent to end at a year high of 1,212.753 points on volume of 1.1 billion shares worth 12 billion yuan ($1.4 billion), the heaviest trade in 1997.
Shenzhen's A index put on 1.8 percent to end at 423.68 points as turnover rose to 12.4 billion yuan from Friday's 8.4 billion.
Brokers said Monday's advance was also linked to Beijing's announcement of a low bank interest rate subsidy for April.
People's Bank of China, the central bank, set the rate at 0.17 percent, down from the March subsidy of 0.94 percent.
"The lower rate indicates the central government's confidence in controlling retail price inflation, which lifted market sentiment," the Guotai analyst said.
On Shanghai's B share market, Shanghai Dazhong Taxi Co was the star on speculative buying, up 8.40 percent to $1.058 on a volume of 60,000 shares.

Meanwhile, Zhongshan Torch High & New Tech Industry Commercial Co was the A share star, also on speculative buying, ending at just under its daily limit-up of 9.97 yuan on volume of 11.2 million shares.
In Shenzhen, Nanshan Power Station was the best B share performer, climbing 8.4 percent to HK$5.68 on volume of 1.01 million shares.
Retailer Chengdu Hualian was the biggest gainer in the A share market, closing the session at 10 percent limit-up of 13.49 yuan on volume of 2.1 million shares.
